results.content:
The immigration raid last week on an electric vehicle battery plant in Georgia owned by two South Korean manufacturers was yet another setback for what had been a fast-growing industry in the United States.

The sector was already beleaguered by lower-than-expected demand for electric vehicles, tariffs on raw materials and the rapid phaseout of a federal tax credit for purchases of E.V.s, which have led companies to delay or scale back production. [...] But the raid at the plant under construction in Ellabell, Ga., which is owned by the carmaker Hyundai and battery supplier LG Energy Solution, raised more risks for foreign manufacturers in the United States. Immigration officials arrested 475 people. Of them, about 300 were South Korean citizens, according to the South Korean foreign minister’s office. [...] Skip to contentSkip to site index

results.title: Battery Pack Tariffs: What OEMs Need to Know in 2026
results.content:
### Mid-2025: The Policy Accelerates

Section 232 investigations into battery-related imports were announced, signaling additional potential tariff actions beyond existing measures. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act eliminated federal EV purchase incentives – the $7,500 new EV tax credit, the $4,000 used EV credit, and the commercial fleet EV credit – reducing downstream demand pressure but doing nothing to reduce upstream input costs for battery manufacturers.

### 2026: FEOC Compliance Kicks In [...] Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) regulations began applying to battery supply chains, creating compliance obligations around Chinese-sourced battery materials that go beyond cost into legal risk territory. We cover FEOC in detail in Section 8. [...] Tariff uncertainty creates strong incentives for longer-term supply agreements that lock in pricing before further tariff escalation. OEMs who signed multi-year battery supply agreements in early 2025, before the worst of the tariff increases took effect, are significantly better positioned than those buying spot. For new programs, discussing long-term pricing frameworks with battery suppliers is now a procurement priority rather than an afterthought.
